summary: Freeze the combined #81/#82 checkpoint transport contract before changing production: raw snapshot bytes must survive CJK/escaped-data chunk boundaries in both directions, malformed foreign/negative/fractional/out-of-range checkpoint chunks must be fatal, and a rejected malformed candidate must leave the prior committed snapshot restorable.
steps: Re-read the current v4 Host checkpoint_chunk receiver, result publication path, Host restore-frame builder, Python restore reader, and Python checkpoint chunk sender after #61 merged.

Froze the successor protocol direction: raw checkpoint bytes will use base64 in both directions, decoded-byte caps will remain authoritative, and the wire protocol version will bump rather than silently changing v4 semantics.

Added real-runtime RED coverage for CJK bytes crossing 128 KiB chunk boundaries, JSON escaping expansion, durable Host-to-kernel restore, and malformed chunk ownership/range checks preserving the previous snapshot.

evidence.note: Confirmed Python slices raw UTF-8 bytes then strict-decodes each chunk, Host slices raw bytes then independently toString('utf8'), and Host checkpoint_chunk validation lacks active-cell identity, safe-integer/range, duplicate/completeness, and aggregate-byte checks.
Production code is intentionally unchanged in this candidate; GitHub Actions will capture the baseline failures before the causal transport patch.

limitations: This record is RED-only evidence and does not claim the issues are fixed.
Durable crash consistency and permissions remain separate #71/#83 concerns even though durable restore is used as a test path here.

summary: Implement private protocol v5 for byte-safe, bounded and strictly validated checkpoint transport. Both Host and Python now carry 128 KiB raw checkpoint chunks as canonical base64, validate sequence ownership/order/count/decoded bytes before publication, and preserve the previous checkpoint on malformed candidates.
steps: Moved the large patch program out of YAML into a temporary standalone guarded Python script after the first inline workflow was rejected by YAML parsing; the rejected workflow created no jobs and changed no production file.

The patch script required unique live-code markers for every replacement, bumped Host/kernel protocol 4 to 5, changed chunk payloads to canonical base64 raw bytes, enforced active-cell id plus safe integer/count/order/duplicate and decoded aggregate limits, validated complete UTF-8 JSON checkpoint bytes before atomic M5 replacement, and cleared accumulator state on terminal paths.

The same one-shot workflow deleted both the temporary patch script and itself, then ran git diff --check, Python py_compile, pnpm typecheck, and the focused checkpoint transport suite before allowing the production commit.

evidence.note: Guarded edits, git diff --check, Python compilation, TypeScript typecheck, focused #81/#82 checkpoint transport suite, and verified commit/push all passed before candidate 6521a9a was created.
This user-authored append-only memory commit triggers the authoritative full matrix on the production candidate.

limitations: Durable checkpoint crash consistency, at-rest permissions and aggregate durable quota remain separate #71/#83/#89 work.
Protocol v5 is intentionally private and fail-closed; mixed v4/v5 Host/kernel files are rejected at the ready handshake rather than attempting wire compatibility.
